home.about: With the blessings of Almighty, Gurus and elders, Sahana Kumar will be performing her formal Vocal Graduation Concert on August 30th, 2026, presented by Paramacharya School of Music under the able guidance of Guru Smt. Geetha Ravi. In the Carnatic classical tradition, this milestone concert represents the culmination of 11 years of rigorous sadhana in Sruti, Laya, Sahitya Bhava, and Manodharma Sangeetham.

vocalist.name: Kum. Sahana Kumar
vocalist.tagline: Incoming Freshman, UC San Diego (ICAM & Cognitive Science) • Disciple of Guru Smt. Geetha Ravi
bio: Kum. Sahana Kumar has been immersed in the sacred tradition of Carnatic classical vocal music for over 11 years under the dedicated and nurturing guidance of Guru Smt. Geetha Ravi at Paramacharya School of Music. Through years of disciplined training, she has developed strong command over pitch, rhythm, and lyrical expression.

Sahana is also an accomplished Bharatanatyam dancer who completed her dance Arangetram in 2024 through Vishwa Shanthi Dance Academy. This rare synergy between dance and music has gifted her a unique holistic appreciation for South Indian classical rhythm, gamakas, and spiritual storytelling.

A graduate of Saratoga High School, Sahana was actively engaged in the performing arts as a member of Choir, Drama, and Musical Theatre, while excelling in the Media Arts Program (MAP) and serving as a Varsity Water Polo goalkeeper.

Sahana will be attending the University of California, San Diego (UCSD), pursuing a dual degree in the interdisciplinary ICAM program (Interdisciplinary Computing and the Arts) and Cognitive Science, bridging technology, human perception, and classical artistic expression.
highlights: 11+ Years Carnatic Vocal Sadhana with Guru Smt. Geetha Ravi
Incoming Freshman, UC San Diego — ICAM & Cognitive Science (Dual Degree)
Saratoga High School Graduate (Choir, Drama, MAP & Varsity Water Polo)

guru.name: Guru Smt. Geetha Ravi
guru.tagline: Acclaimed Musician, Pedagogue & Director, Paramacharya School of Music
bio: Smt. Geetha Ravi is the founder and artistic director of Paramacharya School of Music, where she has cultivated a nurturing environment for students to explore and deepen their connection to Carnatic classical music.

Geetha Ravi is a B-High graded Carnatic vocal artist with All India Radio (AIR Thrissur, Kerala) who has performed extensively across India and the United States, including concerts for prominent Bay Area organizations such as SIFA, Lotus, Swaralahari, and Voice of India. Her musical journey began under the tutelage of her mother, followed by instruction from Smt. Charumathi Ramakrishnan and Sri Vamanan Namboodiri (AIR Staff), and she currently pursues advanced lessons under Sri Neyveli Santhanagopalan. Grounded in both rich traditional lineage and academic rigor, she holds two Master's degrees, most recently completing her second Master's in Music from the University of Madras via correspondence.
highlights: Founder & Artistic Director, Paramacharya School of Music
B-High Graded Carnatic Vocal Artist, All India Radio (AIR Thrissur)
Advanced Studies under Sri Neyveli Santhanagopalan
Two Master's Degrees, including Music from University of Madras

chiefGuest.name: Sangeetha Kalanidhi Sri. Neyveli R. Santhanagopalan
chiefGuest.tagline: Eminent Carnatic Vocalist, Guru, Vidwan & Sangeetha Kalanidhi Awardee
chiefGuest.bio: Sangeetha Kalanidhi Sri. Neyveli R. Santhanagopalan is one of the most revered and accomplished Carnatic vocalists of our era. Renowned for his deep traditionalism, profound knowledge of musicology, and soul-stirring manodharma sangeetham, he has performed across the globe for over four decades. As an extraordinary teacher and cultural ambassador, his gracious presence as Chief Guest bestows immense blessings upon Sahana's graduation concert.

accompanists.name: Kum. Aishwarya Anand
accompanists.guruLineage: Disciple of Guru Smt. Anuradha Sridhar
accompanists.bio: Aishwarya Anand is a vocal and violin disciple of Guru Smt. Anuradha Sridhar, founder and director of Trinity Center for Music, California. Aishwarya is the great granddaughter of Sangita Kalanidhi Sri. T.K. Jayarama Iyer. A highly committed student, she has won several prizes since her childhood including multiple first prizes in the prestigious Cleveland Aradhana. She has been playing full length concerts as an accompanist and in duets with her sister for the past eight years; and participated in several noteworthy collaborative productions with leading artistes, including those produced by her Guru. She also plays western violin and was a part of her college’s philharmonic orchestra. She just completed college at Purdue University and is now working as a silicon design engineer in the semiconductor industry.

accompanists.name: Chi. Anirudh Suresh
accompanists.guruLineage: Disciple of Sri. Ravindra Bharathy Sridharan
accompanists.bio: Anirudh has been learning mridangam for the past 11 years from Sri. Ravindra Bharathy Sridharan, founder and director of Nadhopasana Academy of Fine Arts. In May 2024, he had his mridangam arangetram accompanying Sri. Bharat Sundar, and since then, he has played in the December Margazhi season in various sabhas and is a regular accompanist in the Bay Area and has supported various concerts organized by many different schools. He has also won prizes in the Cleveland Thyagaraja Festival, Sivan competitions, OSAAT, Bay Area Kala Utsavam, and many more. Notably, he placed second in SIFA’s Laya Shresta competition in 2025. Additionally, in 2024, Anirudh was blessed to have been inducted into the prestigious “Hall of Fame” by Life4You. Anirudh has also been learning vocal music for the past 7 years and currently learns from Sri. TN Arunagiri. Anirudh is currently a senior at Milpitas High School.

program.subtitle: The complete curated concert repertoire featuring traditional compositions across Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, and Tamil.

items.title: Viriboni (Bhairavi Ata Thala Varnam)
items.ragam: Bhairavi (Janya of 20th Melakarta Natabhairavi - Bhashanga Ragam)
items.overview: Revered across generations as the 'King of all Varnams' (Varnangalil Raja), 'Viriboni' is the supreme benchmark of vocal discipline, breath control, and rhythmic command in the Carnatic pantheon.
items.details: Composed in the majestic Bhashanga ragam Bhairavi and set to the intricate 14-beat Ata talam, this composition traverses all three octaves. It features structured Purvanga (Pallavi, Anupallavi, Mukthayi Swaram) and Uttaranga (Charanam and four expansive Chittaswara suites) rendered in two speeds (Prathama and Dwitiya Kalam), setting an authoritative, classical tone for the recital.

items.title: Gajavadana Beduve
items.overview: A sparkling invocatory Devaranama in Kannada by the Father of Carnatic Music, Saint Purandara Dasa, offering heartfelt salutations to the elephant-faced Lord Ganesha to remove all obstacles and bestow auspicious blessings.
items.details: Set to the effervescent pentatonic Ragam Hamsadhwani ('the voice of the swan'), this piece radiates spiritual joy and rhythmic symmetry. The composition features vibrant Kalpanaswarams (spontaneous swara permutations) that invigorate the concert atmosphere.

items.title: Jnanamosagarada (Sub-Main)
items.overview: The Sub-Main centerpiece of the first half. A profound philosophical masterpiece by Saint Tyagaraja beseeching Lord Rama: 'Will You not bestow upon me supreme wisdom (Jnana) and the path of divine truth?'
items.details: Poorvikalyani is renowned for its intense emotional depth (gambhiram) and prathi madhyama curves. The presentation includes an elaborate Raga Alapana delineating hallmark phrases, followed by the kriti with brisk Neraval at 'Paramathmudu' and multi-speed kalpanaswaras concluding in a synchronized makutam.

items.title: Ananda Natana Prakasam
items.overview: One of the monumental Pancha Bhoota Sthala Kritis representing the Element of Ether/Space (Akasa Lingam) at the sacred temple of Chidambaram.
items.details: Composed in majestic Sanskrit by Muthuswami Dikshitar, this grand kriti vividly describes Lord Shiva's cosmic dance of bliss (Ananda Tandavam) in the Golden Hall of Chidambaram. The stately vakra phrases of Ragam Kedaram paired with the rhythmic 7-beat Misra Chapu talam evoke cosmic majesty and deep spiritual wonder.

items.title: Bhogendra Sayinam
items.overview: A buoyant, melodious Sanskrit composition by the royal composer Maharaja Swathi Thirunal extolling Lord Vishnu reclining peacefully upon the celestial serpent king, Adisesha.
items.details: The unique scalar contours of Ragam Kuntalavarali (omitting Rishabham and Gandharam) combined with the lively 5-beat Khanda Chapu cycle create an undulating, wavy rhythm that mirrors the gentle sway of the ocean of milk (Ksheerasagara), complemented by cascading chittaswaras.

items.title: Sarojadala Netri (Grand Main Centerpiece)
items.overview: The crowning zenith and monumental centerpiece of the concert. Syama Sastri's 'Sarojadala Netri' is one of the grandest gems in Carnatic music, praising the lotus-eyed Goddess Meenakshi with unmatched rhythmic architecture and lyrical majesty.
items.details: This centerpiece unfolds through structured classical Manodharma: an expansive multi-octave Raga Alapana across Mandra, Madhya, and Tara sthayis, majestic pulse-driven Tanam, thematic Neraval at 'Sama Gana Vinodini', mathematically intricate kalpanaswaras in 2-kalai Adi talam, and an exhilarating Tani Avartanam percussion solo.

items.title: ArabhiManam
items.overview: An expressive, soulful composition set as a vibrant Ragamalika (a garland of diverse ragas), conveying heartfelt devotion and seeking divine grace and affection (Abhimanam).
items.details: Rendered as a melodious Ragamalika, this piece seamlessly traverses contrasting melodic colors and moods, sustaining a joyful, devotional cadence following the grand centerpiece.

items.title: Andru Ivulagam (Thiruppavai Pasuram 24)
items.composer: Kotai Nachiyar (Sri Andal) • Music: Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar
items.overview: The celebrated 24th Pasuram of Andal's sacred Tamil Thiruppavai, singing praises of Lord Vishnu's cosmic footsteps measuring the entire universe (Trivikrama Avatara): 'Praise be to Thy feet that measured this whole world of yore!'
items.details: Rendered in the deeply emotional and universal raga Sindhu Bhairavi, this piece captures Andal's sublime surrender and unconditional bhakti through delicate gamakas and melodious devotional poetry.

items.title: Valli Kanavan Perai (Kavadi Chindu)
items.overview: The infectious, pulsating folk-classical Kavadi Chindu dedicated to Lord Muruga: 'Chant the name of Valli's consort, oh parrot, and sing His eternal glories!'
items.details: Characterized by lilting syncopated rhythms (Tisra Nadai) and joyful, catchy refrains, this piece shifts the concert mood from heavy classical manodharma into soulful, spirited regional folk traditions.

items.title: Maand Thillana
items.overview: The rhythmic crescendo and aesthetic climax of the concert. Composed by the legendary violin maestro Lalgudi G. Jayaraman in the lilting, sweet Ragam Mand (Maand).
items.details: Driven by crisp rhythmic sollukattus (percussive syllables like 'Ta Dhim Ta Na'), brisk swara passages, and playful cross-rhythmic syncopations, this piece delivers an exhilarating, synchronized finale filled with celebratory ecstasy.

items.title: Harivarasanam & Pavamana Mangalam
items.deity: Lord Ayyappa, Sri Rama & Universal Peace
items.overview: The sacred conclusion of the concert. It begins with 'Harivarasanam', the celestial lullaby sung every night at the Sabarimala sanctum, and concludes with the auspicious Tyagaraja Mangalam 'Pavamana'.
items.details: Rendered in the supreme peace of Ragam Madhyamavathi—which according to tradition dissolves any tonal imbalances and leaves only harmony—the recital concludes with prayers of gratitude to the Gurus, ancestors, and rasikas for universal peace and prosperity.
